story.title: Presley Gerber, son of Cindy Crawford, passes away at 27
story.summary: Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, has died at the age of 27. His death occurred at a rehabilitation facility in Los Angeles, as confirmed by a family representative. The family has requested privacy during this difficult time.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the cause of death?
explore_lenses.title: Cause and manner remain unreported
explore_lenses.summary: The death and location have been confirmed, but the available official and local reporting did not provide a cause or manner of death. Reporting should not treat the rehabilitation setting as proof of why he died.

claims.text: Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records cited by local outlets say Gerber died on September 20, 2026, at a rehabilitation facility; the publicly available reporting did not list a cause of death.
NBC Los Angeles reported that an autopsy had not yet been completed and that a cause of death was not immediately available.

explore_lenses.label: Does the rehab setting explain what happened?
explore_lenses.title: Treatment location is not a determination
explore_lenses.summary: The setting establishes where Gerber died, not the medical or legal explanation for the death. His previously public discussions of addiction and mental health provide background, but they do not establish a connection to this death.

claims.text: ABC News reported that Gerber had publicly discussed mental-health and substance-use struggles and treatment, including a 2024 video series; it also reported that further cause-of-death details were unavailable.
Kaia Gerber had described her brother's public openness about addiction as meaningful to their family, according to ABC's account of her Vogue interview.
The family representative asked for privacy and characterized the period as difficult and painful.

explore_lenses.label: What official findings could come next?
explore_lenses.title: Medical examiner findings are the key next record
explore_lenses.summary: The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner is the relevant authority for a formal cause-and-manner determination. Its published guidance says autopsy and toxicology work can inform those determinations, but the reviewed sources did not provide a timeline for Gerber's case.

claims.text: The county medical examiner defines cause of death as the injury or disease ultimately leading to death, while manner of death classifies how it came about, including natural, accident, suicide, homicide, or undetermined.
The county says postmortem toxicology examines specimens for drugs, toxins, and poisons to help determine cause and manner of death.
The medical examiner says case information placed on its site is public record, subject to California public-records law, though some security-hold cases are not displayed.

story_report.summary: Presley Gerber, the 27-year-old son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, died Sept. 20, 2026, at a Los Angeles rehabilitation facility, according to county medical-examiner records cited in local reporting. A family representative described the period as difficult and painful and requested privacy. An autopsy had not yet been completed when NBC Los Angeles reported on the death, and no cause of death was immediately available.

sections.heading: Presley Gerber’s Public Recovery Discussions
sections.body: ABC News reported that Gerber had spoken publicly about mental-health and substance-use struggles and treatment, including in a 2024 video series. The network also reported that his sister, Kaia Gerber, had said in a Vogue interview that his openness about addiction had been meaningful to their family. Neither account attributes his death to addiction, treatment, medication or another specific factor.

sections.heading: Los Angeles County Death Review
sections.body: The Los Angeles County medical examiner distinguishes cause of death—the injury or disease ultimately leading to death—from manner of death, which may be classified as natural, accident, suicide, homicide or undetermined. The county says postmortem toxicology tests specimens for drugs, toxins and poisons to help establish those findings. Case information posted by the examiner is public record, subject to California public-records law.

unresolved.text: Public reporting reviewed did not provide a cause or manner of death, an autopsy-completion date, toxicology results, or a timeline for final findings.

related_stories.title: Charles Spencer Accuses King Charles of Gaslighting Over Diana Memoir
related_stories.summary: Charles Spencer, the brother of Princess Diana, has accused King Charles III of 'gaslighting' him regarding his recollections of events surrounding Diana's death. This accusation comes ahead of the release of Spencer's memoir, where he claims the King was 'giddily elated' shortly after Diana's passing. The controversy has sparked significant discussion in the UK as the memoir's publication approaches.
